Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments Co.Ltd (ZEMIC)"
Document: "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments Co. Ltd."

The difference: register has "Co.Ltd" (no space), document has "Co. Ltd." (with space). Also register includes "(ZEMIC)" abbreviation.

Rules say: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift = same-entity. Best value... For same-entity, what's the best value? The rules don't explicitly say for same-entity, but the fused record should carry the cleaner form. The document is the legal instrument; "Co. Ltd." is the properly spaced legal-suffix form. The register adds "(ZEMIC)" abbreviation which is useful. Hmm.

The rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." Then "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." So for numbers/years, register's canonical form. For names, presumably best value is... the document's since certificate is the legal instrument? But that rule was specified for different-entity. For same-entity, the choice is less specified. The document is the legal instrument, so the document's form "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments Co. Ltd." with proper spacing seems best. Alternatively, one could argue the register's includes the abbreviation (ZEMIC) which is helpful metadata, but the best_value for the applicant field should be the legal name.

I'll say: verdict "same-entity", best_value "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments Co. Ltd." — the document's properly punctuated legal name, since document is the legal instrument and only differs by spacing; (ZEMIC) abbreviation is extra alias in register, not conflict. Actually the best_value could optionally preserve the alias, but the field is applicant name; the document's form is the authoritative name.
